parsed.same_study_reason: Both lists discuss a paper on cross-country pharmaceutical pricing, GDP, and contributions to R&D as a public good. B2 cites Frech et al. 2022, consistent with the RAND price-index, quasi-rent framework in List A.

pairs.reason: Both argue the GDP elasticity/correlation does not test strategic R&D contribution. It may instead reflect general willingness to pay for health or drug spending rising with income. B1 also frames this as omitted-variable bias.

Both target the main GDP regression and say it does not identify the hypothesized behavior. A10 calls the result mechanical, because the contribution measure scales with spending. B1 instead points to omitted variables and willingness to pay for current health.
Both question whether the GDP correlation supports the theoretical interpretation. A12 concerns the lack of testable implications that would discriminate among models, not confounding.
